prize_parts.citation: For incorporating firm heterogeneity into trade theory, showing how selection into exporting and foreign investment and reallocation across firms shape the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B010 as a single part, credited to Helpman and Melitz. I reassessed it against the round-1 exchange and the chair's questions. Three things keep it first for me. First, it pairs a new fact base with a framework that explains it. Firm-level data showed that exporters are rare and systematically different. Melitz (2003) supplied a tractable model of selection into exporting, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extended it to the choice between exporting and foreign investment. That combination of data discovery and explanatory framework is the criterion I weigh most. Second, the mechanism has more than twenty years of testing across many countries, and it is used in empirical trade, in macro and labour applications and in liberalisation analysis, so maturity is not in doubt. Third, the credit line is comparatively short and defensible. On distinctness from 2008, the chair asked which predictions representative-firm new trade theory does not generate. Those predictions are: only a subset of firms export; exporters are larger and more productive than non-exporters before they enter; liberalisation induces exit of the least productive firms and reallocation toward the most productive; aggregate productivity rises through that reallocation; and productivity sorts firms across domestic sales, exporting and foreign investment. Symmetric-firm models are silent on all of these. The qualitative selection and reallocation result does not depend on Pareto productivity draws, though the size of the gains does. I would therefore have the citation rest on the mechanism and not on any welfare number. I do not treat the convergence of eight members on the same pair as scientific merit. It tells me only that independent assessors draw the attribution boundary in the same place.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still credit. Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, and Hopenhayn on firm dynamics, documented key facts or built closely related models, and none is credited on this ballot. Wording the citation narrowly and acknowledging them in the scientific background reduces that cost but does not remove it. Second, the quantitative gains-from-trade magnitudes are sensitive to distributional assumptions. As I recall it, later quantitative work shows that under some assumptions the welfare formulas coincide with those of models without selection, which limits how much of the welfare story is specific to heterogeneity. I have not independently verified this. Third, trade was recognised in 2008, and the Committee must be satisfied that this is a distinct advance. I think it is, but Boppart's file treats the concern as not fully resolved, and I do not claim to have settled it for him. Finally, I come from an empirical labour field and may tilt toward candidates whose predictions are confronted with micro data. That tilt favours B010, so I record it as a possible bias.

responses.point: Boppart keeps B019 (Kiyotaki and Moore) as his preferred part. He now treats B010 as a serious alternative, but he cites B010's contested credit with Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum and the cleaner single-mechanism attribution of B019.
responses.response: I accept that B019 has the cleaner credit line, with two originators and a single 1997 mechanism, and I see it as a real advantage over B010. Where we differ is on weighting. The chair's summary says B019 supporters weigh a clean single mechanism more heavily than a larger body of confirming evidence. I give more weight to how directly the mechanism has been identified in data. B010's predictions on exporter premia, entry and exit, and reallocation have been tested directly on firm-level data. B019's amplification channel is mostly inferred indirectly, and the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises is thematically adjacent. I read the B010 precursor problem as a wording and background-acknowledgement issue. The selection mechanism has an identifiable origin in Melitz (2003), and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple has the same standing for the exporting-versus-FDI extension. I would not oppose B019 on merit if the Committee finds it distinct from 2022. My preference between the two rests on the quality of identification, not on a view that his case is weak.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B019 first but says he is not fully settled on the order of B019 and B010. He accepts that B010 has a mature empirical record and unusually uniform attribution, and that the 2022 overlap and weaker direct identification count against B019.
responses.response: His candour on those two weaknesses is where I agree with him most, and it is the main reason I stay with B010. His distinction between 2022 and Kiyotaki-Moore is reasonable: bank runs and intermediation are different mechanisms from collateral-value feedback in the real economy. But thematic adjacency is a cost the Committee has to defend, whereas B010's cost is credit for precursors, which can be handled in the scientific background. I also take his point that B010's agreement across members is not additional evidence of merit. I am relying on the substance, not on the count. His two-name boundary for B019 is the cleanest option, and if the Committee prefers it I would regard the choice as a defensible weighting of attribution against identification, not an error.

responses.point: Enflo prefers B032 with Autor, Hanson and Dorn, having dropped Katz. She argues that the causal evidence on local labour-market adjustment has been stress-tested for a decade and that continued debate over magnitudes shows the findings have been scrutinised, not that they are fragile.
responses.response: I agree with her on that last point, and it applies equally to B010, where debate over magnitudes does not undermine the qualitative mechanism. As a labour economist I value B032's transparent designs and its reach into political and distributional questions. That is why it stays on my alternatives list. I still rank it below B010 for three reasons. The entry bundles two strands, the task framework and the trade-shock empirics, and the Committee would have to choose one before it can name people. Shift-share identification and the persistence of effects are still actively contested. Credit for the task framework reaches Acemoglu, Restrepo, Levy and Murnane. On the third name, her narrowing to Dorn is sensible if the trade-shock strand is the core. I proposed only Autor and Hanson in round 1, and I still think two names is the more conservative reading. I disclose that my field is close to hers, and that proximity could make me more generous to B032 than a neutral reader would be.

responses.point: Hassler (chair) ranks B010 first. He wants the citation kept to the firm-heterogeneity discovery, not a career-wide framing for Helpman, and he excludes Redding from the core because his contribution is quantitative and spatial trade built on this base. He also notes Bernard-Jensen deserve recognition for the exporter facts.
responses.response: I agree with the narrow framing and with leaving Redding out of the core pair. Answering the chair's question on Redding: I know of no contribution of his that originates the selection mechanism, so a third name would change the attribution without strengthening it. On Bernard and Jensen, I would acknowledge the exporter facts in the scientific background and keep the citation on the explanatory model. Hassler himself concedes that the facts motivated the theory but did not supply the unifying model. I would go one step further on wording, by naming selection and foreign investment together with reallocation. The Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple strand is what justifies Helpman's inclusion beyond a lifetime framing. I note that Hassler is the chair and one of the eight B010 supporters, and I do not read his position as additional evidence.

responses.point: Andersson prefers B010 but keeps B003 as his main alternative. He describes B003 as scientifically strong but with narrower support and a harder boundary question over Bresnahan, Reiss and Benkard.
responses.response: I share his view of B003 and keep it as my first alternative for the same reason: the Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes core is the cleanest credit structure on an empirical-methods entry, and the methods are standard in antitrust and regulation. I would not combine it with B010 as a second part. B010 uses two of the three permitted names, so a BLP trio would require a partial credit that I find unsatisfactory. I also see the chair's question of whether B003 is a methods award or a substantive discovery about market power as unresolved. Until the Bresnahan boundary and that framing are settled, I would not rank B003 above B010.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee accepts that selection and reallocation are a distinct advance beyond the 2008 recognition, and whether Boppart's remaining concern is answered by the testable-predictions argument.
How to word the citation and the scientific background so that Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum and Hopenhayn are acknowledged without widening the laureate set.
How much of the size of the selection gains survives alternative productivity distributions, and whether later quantitative work narrows what is specific to heterogeneity.

Whether the weight I put on direct empirical identification over attribution clarity is the right weighting between B010 and B019. Reasonable members weigh it differently, and I would not call the question settled.
My assessments rely on my own recollection of the literature and on colleagues' round-1 statements. I have not independently verified citation, replication or policy-use claims.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Helpman, Melitz or any other credited name on B010 is apparent from my supplied profile. My frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited on any alternative I list. I disclose field proximity to labour economics, and so to B032, which is one of my alternatives, with no documented personal or co-authorship connection to its credited names. I am a co-opted member whose profile documents no connection to the trade candidates. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
